messages.subject: Deployment issues with library(randomForestSRC)
parts:
I am working on an app that takes a model (saved to an .rda object) to predict an outcome variable. It works beautifully locally with no error, however when I deploy to shinyapps I get this message:

An error has occurred in prediction.  Please turn trace on for further analysis.

You can see it running live:

https://vsoch.shinyapps.io/prostate

To debug - I re-generated the model on my personal rstudio (it was done on another machine) and also have eliminated reading the variables in from the interface (I hard coded in values) and it doesn't seem to help. I can't figure out what might be different in the cloud / shinyapps environment than my local machine, so I am hoping to get help from this list.  You can see the full code for my app in the page (I use www/index.html instead of ui.R) and the server.R is as follows:

library(randomForestSRC)
load("model.rda")
palette(c("#E41A1C", "#377EB8", "#4DAF4A", "#984EA3",
          "#FF7F00", "#FFFF33", "#A65628", "#F781BF", "#999999"))
shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  # Combine the selected variables into a new data frame
  data = reactive({
    data = c()
    data$race = switch(input$race,
                   white = 1,
                   black = 2,
                   1)
   
    data$psa = as.numeric(input$psa)
    data$age = input$age
    data$svi = input$svi
    data$sm = input$sm
    data$bmi = input$bmi
    data$lni = input$lni
    data$rpyear = input$year
    data$ece = as.numeric(input$ece)
    data$pg1 = as.numeric(input$pg1)
    data$pg2 = as.numeric(input$pg2)
    data
  })
  output$summary = renderTable({
  
  #data = data()    
  X = c()
  X$rpyear = 1995 #data$rpyear
  X$PSA = 3.5 #data$psa
  X$race = 1 #data$race
  X$age = 44 #data$age
  X$pG1 = 0 #data$pg1
  X$pG2 = 0 #data$pg2
  X$SVI = 0 #data$svi
  X$SM = 0 #data$sm
  X$ECE = 0 #data$ece
  X$BMI = 17.2#data$bmi
  X$LNI = 0#data$lni
  X$time = NULL
  X$event = NULL
  X$X10yrOutcome = NULL
  X$chf.oob1 = NULL
  X$chf.oob2 = NULL
  X$S = NULL
  X$cif1 = NULL
  X$cif2 = NULL
  X$M1 = NULL
  X$M2 = NULL
  X$EST = NULL
  X$k_r = NULL
  X$time1 = NULL
  X$time2 = NULL
  table(X)
  prediction = predict(rsf.cr, as.data.frame(X))
  CIF.1 = as.numeric(prediction$cif[,which(prediction$time.interest == 120),1])
  CIF.2 = as.numeric(prediction$cif[,which(prediction$time.interest == 120),2])
  result = c(CIF.1,CIF.2)
  table(result)
  
  })
  
})
I also tried adding a pause, in the case that there was some weirdness with trying to predict without proper time to load the Rda.  My guess is that it has something to do with data types / structures (because R is just like that) but I'm not sure how to go about testing. I'd be happy to provide whatever info would be helpful for testing, and try things as well. Thanks for the help!

library(randomForestSRC)
load("model.rda")
palette(c("#E41A1C", "#377EB8", "#4DAF4A", "#984EA3",

  # Combine the selected variables into a new data frame

    data = c()
    data$race = switch(input$race,
                   white = 1,
                   black = 2,
                   1)
   
    data$psa = as.numeric(input$psa)
    data$age = input$age

    data$bmi = input$bmi
    data$lni = input$lni
    data$rpyear = input$year
    data$ece = as.numeric(input$ece)
    data$pg1 = as.numeric(input$pg1)
    data$pg2 = as.numeric(input$pg2)
    data
  })

  #data = data()
